title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing (Q2 2026)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
========

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design notes, roadmap themes, pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product line for Q2 2026. Intended audience: product managers, engineering leads (runtime, infra, SRE), solutions engineering, go-to-market, and customer success.

Summary / TL;DR
----------------
- Product: Unified Inference — a single developer experience and runtime that unifies Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments.
- Goal this quarter: stabilize the v2.1 runtime, ship per-route quality monitoring, introduce a tiered pricing model for dedicated reservations, and roll out automated model fallback policies for cross-region reliability.
- Key success metrics: reduce median p95-generation latency by 12% across common workloads, decrease hosted cost-per-1000-tokens by 8% via batching improvements, and secure three Dedicated commitments >= $100k ARR.

Goals & Non-goals
------------------
Goals (Q2 2026):
1. Deliver per-route quality monitoring and regression alerts in Redwood Console (MVP).
2. Implement Model Routing: cost-aware fallback feature with canary rollouts.
3. Publish pricing & packaging for Dedicated tiers (Standard/Enterprise).
4. Improve runtime kernel selection heuristics to reduce token cost.

Non-goals: full multi-tenant GPU migration, new large-model pretraining, replacing existing KMS integrations.

Target users
------------
- ML/Platform engineers at mid-market and enterprise customers (primary).
- Product engineers building LLM features (secondary).
- Platform teams evaluating SLA-backed inference with predictable cost.

Success metrics (KPIs)
----------------------
- Reliability: Hosted API availability >= 99.95% (monthly).
- Latency: median p95 generation latency <= target by model class (see SLO table).
- Cost: reduce average token cost by 8% for hosted customers via optimizer suggestions.
- Revenue: onboard minimum 3 new Dedicated customers with annual commitments >= $100k each.

SLO & Thresholds (runtime & API)
--------------------------------
| Service | SLI | SLO | Alert threshold | Owner |
| Hosted inference (API) | successful requests (5xx rate) | <0.1% errors monthly | >0.2% for 15m | eng-sre |
| Latency (p95 tokens gen) | p95 latency per call | <= 450ms (short prompts), <= 1.8s (long prompts) | >550ms / >2.2s | eng-serving-runtime |
| Dedicated capacity availability | uptime | >= 99.9% monthly | < 99.7% | eng-platform |
| Model routing correctness | percent correctly routed | >= 99% | < 97% | eng-serving-runtime |

NOTE: Thresholds are applied per-region. All alerts emit to #sre-inference and create Pagertree incidents for severity >= P1.

Product Requirements (MUST / SHOULD / COULD)
--------------------------------------------
MUST:
- Per-route quality monitoring (MUST capture prompt set metrics: BLEU / ROUGE / embedding-similarity baseline, failure rate, hallucination rate).
- Model routing policy engine (MUST be able to route by latency, cost, and region).
- Console: expose per-route token-level cost and latency breakdowns.
- API: backward-compatible endpoints for generate/chat/embeddings.

SHOULD:
- Autosuggest quantization profiles for model workloads.
- Integrate regressions into CI (pull-request gating for model-rollouts).

COULD:
- Built-in prompt-store with versioning and diff support.
- Pre-baked prompt templates for common verticals (search, summarization, chat).

Requirements table (condensed)
------------------------------
| ID | Title | Priority | Owner | Acceptance criteria |
| PRD-01 | Per-route quality monitoring | MUST | Product / Applied ML | Console shows baseline + recent metrics; alerts when regression > 5% for 24h; documented API for metric export. |
| PRD-02 | Model routing & fallback | MUST | Eng - Serving Runtime | Policy engine routes requests per-config; automatic fallback to compatible model variant within 300ms when capacity constrained; audit logs for routing decisions. |
| PRD-03 | Dedicated pricing tiers | MUST | Product / Finance | Published pricing page, sales playbook, and billing integration test coverage. |

Design & High-level Architecture
--------------------------------
Introduction: Unified Inference layers the following components: Control Plane (routing, policy, billing), Serving Runtime (GPU-optimized inference engine), Observability (metrics/traces/evals), and Deployment Abstraction (hosted/dedicated/private).

Key design decisions:
- Keep the API contract stable: v1 endpoints remain compatible; introduce fields for routing hints.
- Routing policy engine is policy-first: policies are JSON-based and declarative.
- Use continuous batching + KV cache to reduce token costs while honoring latency SLOs.

Runtime components (responsibilities):
- Inference Worker: executes model kernels, exposes /metrics and /kv-cache endpoints.
- Router Service: performs policy evaluation and selects target worker(s).
- Cache Layer: global prefix/KV cache with LRU eviction and per-customer isolation.
- Metrics Collector: emits per-token traces to telemetry backend (owned by eng-platform).

Sequence (simplified):
1. Client => Redwood API (hosted) with route tag.
2. Router evaluates policy; selects a model variant.
3. Router checks cache; if miss, forwards to Inference Worker.
4. Worker streams tokens back; Cache updated.
5. Telemetry emitted for cost/latency/quality signals.

API Contract (example - generate)
--------------------------------
Request (JSON):
{
  "model": "redwood-unified-1.3",
  "route": "support-chat",
  "input": "<user prompt>",
  "timeout_ms": 30000,
  "routing_hints": { "prefer_low_cost": true }
}

Response (streamed chunk example):
{ "chunk": "...token...", "metadata": { "model_variant": "redwood-unified-1.3-q4", "latency_ms": 45 } }

CLI example (admin)
-------------------
# Create a routing policy (example)
redwoodctl policy create --name "support-low-cost" --json '{"rules":[{"when":{"route":"support"},"then":{"prefer":"low_cost","fallback":"regional-compatible"}}]}'

Design constraints & tradeoffs
-------------------------------
- Policy evaluation must be fast (<2ms median) or it will add unacceptable overhead. We use precompiled decision trees in the router.
- Caching improves cost but increases correctness risk for stateful prompts; cache is disabled for routes marked stateful.

Roadmap & Themes (next 6 months)
--------------------------------
Q2 2026 (now) - Stabilization & Packaging:
- Ship per-route quality monitoring (MVP) and regression alerts.
- Dedicated pricing tiers and sales enablement.
- Canary Model Routing and fallback.

Q3 2026 - Optimization & Scale:
- Autosuggest batching/quantization configs in console.
- Improve kernel selection for long-sequence workloads.
- Private deployment GA for select regulated customers.

Q4 2026 - Enterprise & Observability:
- Advanced evals integration into CI/CD.
- Rolling upgrades for dedicated pools with zero-downtime migrations.

Dependency list
---------------
- eng-serving-runtime: kernel & scheduler updates (owner: Priya Nair).
- eng-platform: metrics/console integrations (owner: Marco Li).
- finance-and-legal: pricing signoff and contract templates (owner: Sarah Kline).

Pricing & Packaging Notes (summary)
----------------------------------
Pricing principles: transparent, usage-aligned, and predictable for Dedicated. Offer clear trade-offs between cost and latency/SLOs.

Hosted (Self-serve):
- Generation: $0.006 per 1k tokens (short model), $0.012 per 1k tokens (long-context models).
- Embeddings: $0.02 per 1k embeddings units.
- Free tier: 50k tokens / month for first 30 days.

Dedicated (Reserved capacity):
- Tiers: Standard (monthly commitment >= $10k), Enterprise (monthly commitment >= $50k).
- Pricing: commit-based blended rate (e.g., Standard: $0.004 per 1k tokens equivalent at 1x baseline utilization).
- Overcommit: burst buffer available at premium per-token rate (1.5x committed rate).
- SLA: 99.9% uptime, 24/7 priority support (Enterprise).

Private (VPC / On-prem):
- License + support model: one-time platform fee + annual support (negotiated).
- KMS/HSM integration and audit log packages offered as add-ons.

Sales playbook highlights:
1. Qualification: target companies with >$1M ARR and inference workloads >100M tokens/month.
2. Demo: show per-route cost & latency dashboards, model routing failover, and regression alerts.
3. Contract: include migration credit (first 3 months).

Packaging examples (customer scenarios)
--------------------------------------
- Startup (Self-serve): typically Hosted with pay-as-you-go, uses optimizer suggestions to lower cost.
- Scale-up (Hybrid): Dedicated for core workloads, Hosted for burst/experimentation.
- Enterprise (Private): Private deployment + Dedicated for split workloads.

Release Notes (2026-05-15 release)
----------------------------------
Release version: unified-inference-v2.1.0
Highlights:
- Per-route quality monitoring (MVP) exposed in Console with baseline comparisons and regression alerts.
- Model Routing: initial cost-aware routing with fallback to regional-compatible model variants.
- Dedicated pricing tiers published; billing integration for Standard & Enterprise tested.

Detailed changes:
- eng-serving-runtime: kernel selector updated (v2.1-ks1) — improves long-seq throughput by ~10%. (Owner: Priya Nair)
- Router service: policy language v1 (json-declarative) and audit logging. (Owner: Omar Reyes)
- Console: UI panels for per-route quality and token-cost breakdown. (Owner: Marco Li)

Migration & Rollout Plan
------------------------
1. Internal rollout (week 0): feature flag enabled in staging, verify telemetry and console integration.
2. Canary (week 1): enable for 5% of traffic on hosted API (routes: support-chat, doc-summarize).
3. Metrics gate: rollout to 25% only if p95 latency delta <= +10% and error rate delta <= +0.05%.
4. Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% (each step 48–72 hours with monitoring).
5. Dedicated customers: 2-week coordinated rollout with account teams; run migration dry-run.

Rollback criteria:
- Increase in 5xx rate > 0.2% sustained for 30 minutes.
- p95 latency exceed target by >20% for 60 minutes.
- Two or more customers report unresolved correctness regressions.

Operational runbook (brief)
---------------------------
- Who to page: #sre-inference on Slack; PagerDuty escalation for P1.
- Quick checks: Router logs for decision latencies, worker /metrics, KV cache hit rate, telemetry pipeline lag.
- Recovery: disable routing policy via feature flag; force routing to stable fallback model.

Open risks & mitigations
------------------------
- Risk: Caching could return stale completions for stateful flows. Mitigation: explicit route-level "stateful" flag disables caching; add warning in Console.
- Risk: Pricing complexity confuses buyers. Mitigation: publish clear examples, break-even calculators, and sales playbook.
- Risk: Policy engine performance regression. Mitigation: precompile rules and run load tests as part of CI.
